Why do a triangle's three angles always add up to one hundred eighty degrees?
Here is a proof you can see.
Take any triangle, and mark its three corners.
Line them up, corner to corner.
They fit together perfectly, and make a straight line.
A straight line is half a turn. That is one hundred eighty degrees.
Here is another way. Draw a line through the top, parallel to the bottom.
The corner on the left has an identical twin up at the top.
So does the corner on the right.
Together with the top corner, three angles fill a straight line.
So the three angles add up to one hundred eighty degrees. Always.
